headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can exfiltrate shared business data if paired with Spring Integration workflows that pass outputs onward; other risks are lower due to limited overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between airbyte and spring-integration-samples, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. Airbyte has broad network egress and Spring Integration is an integration sample set, so a manual copy/paste or file bridge could exist, but that is unusual and the blast radius is small without a documented shared parser.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies Airbyte output into a Spring Integration flow as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw Airbyte output into Spring Integration routes.
Add a provenance prefix to any transferred text.
Review any shared queue or file bridge before use.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, while spring-integration-samples has no documented egress but is an integration-oriented project. A shared workspace or handoff could leak business data from Airbyte into downstream outputs; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs business data into a shared workspace consumed by Spring Integration, leakage is possible.
IF Spring Integration is configured to forward received payloads to external systems, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Restrict Airbyte exports to least-necessary fields.
Disable any downstream forwarding in Spring Integration.
Audit logs for business-data fields before transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can egress broadly, but spring-integration-samples shows no write, OAuth, or network capability beyond being an integration sample. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so capability conflict is limited to unusual shared-resource setups rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource, conflicts may occur.
IF Spring Integration is extended with write access to the same destination Airbyte uses, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct destinations per agent.
Avoid shared credentials.
Add locking around any shared mutable resource.
Verify write targets before enabling either workflow.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and Spring Integration samples are designed to move messages between systems. If Spring Integration treats Airbyte output as authoritative without validation, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pathway is inferred from their roles, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Spring Integration consumes Airbyte output without schema or semantic validation, errors can propagate.
IF downstream routes trigger actions from that payload, the impact expands.
mitigations: Validate schema at the handoff.
Insert a human review step for critical records.
Reject malformed or unexpected fields.
Log and compare source-versus-transformed records.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad egress, but neither profile documents regulated data classes, residency, or retention mismatches. Spring Integration samples show no special compliance surface. With only docs-level evidence, compliance risk is limited to undocumented deployment choices rather than a default violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Airbyte into a noncompliant Spring Integration deployment, a breach may occur.
IF retention or residency settings differ between the two systems, compliance drift is possible.
mitigations: Classify data before routing.
Confirm residency settings on both sides.
Disable logging of payload contents.
Document retention for each hop.
